correctness_bisect.note: check_mimo_cuda.py's 658-token prompt in 256-row blocks: the k10 engine failed the check; each probe reran its CUDA side (probe.py) with the settings shown, against the same CPU logits. k10 summed FP8's and MXFP4's products in one FMA chain with the scales folded into the weights; k11 is k10 with each scale group's products summed apart.

probes.what: the check itself: every GPU prompt path on
the experts through the cache only
the attention's rows down and up between the matrices
only the matrices on the GPU, tiled
only the matrices on the GPU, the decode kernels' (one warp a row)
every path on, the scaled formats' sums by scale group (the fix)

decode_fix.what: matmul_piece asked the driver (cudaPointerGetAttributes, twice) on every matrix call whether the caller's buffers were pinned, to send a prompt block's straight; a decode step's calls paid it too
decode_fix.before: benchmark/before-*: r2's engine 2.623 tok/s (median; decode 3.24), this round's 2.578 (3.20); the CUDA matmuls' wall time over the benchmark's 14,208 calls: FP8 4.466 -> 4.573 s, packed bf16 2.137 -> 2.278 s
decode_fix.after: only a prompt block's (tiled) calls ask: benchmark/1-4, r2's 2.607 and 2.619 against 2.621 and 2.617 (decode 3.22 - 3.24 both); the check's GPU logits the same bytes as before the change

dead_ends.what: blocks of 128 x 256, 8 x 16 a thread (a third fewer shared-memory reads a product, one block an SM)
four 64-output groups a thread block (NG=4) for the o_proj and qkv
dead_ends.result: no clear gain over two (within the bench's 10% noise): reverted

dead_ends.what: the experts' outputs copied down by the copy engine once their kernels were done, polled, or by a narrow store kernel
dead_ends.result: 1.8 - 2.5 ms an expert against 1.65 for the down kernel storing them into pinned memory itself (tools/bench_mimo_moe.cu): the slots waited on the copies

dead_ends.what: a free slot chosen for each expert instead of the slots in turn
FP8 / MXFP4 sums in one FMA chain, the scales folded into the weights (k1..k10)
dead_ends.result: about 10% faster for the qkv (40 against 36.5 TFLOP/s) but ten times less accurate (2.5e-7 of the products' magnitude against 2.6e-8): the argmax left the CPU's at 7 of 658 positions with only the matrices tiled (max KL 0.36) and at 36 with everything (max KL 7.5)
